neighbours.label: Degree or pre-article expressions at the point where an article must follow: "by⟦ far⟧ the best", "somewhat⟦ of⟧ an", "⟦ such⟧ an", weaker "more of a", "called a", "quite a"
fire: The lemon tart was by far the most popular dish at the fair.
My uncle has become somewhat of an expert on old clocks.
I had never seen such an enormous pumpkin before that day.
Among the candidates she was by far the strongest speaker.
The old lighthouse is somewhat of a landmark for local sailors.
Nobody expected such a quiet boy to win the debate.
Of all the routes we tried, this one was by far the shortest.
The new teacher turned out to be somewhat of a perfectionist.
quiet: The lemon tart stall was not far from the gate of the fair.
My uncle has become somewhat forgetful about winding old clocks.
I had never seen pumpkins of that size before that day.
Among the candidates, as far as I could tell, she spoke best.
The old lighthouse is one of many landmarks for local sailors.
Nobody expected such things from the quiet boy in the debate.
So far we have tried three of the routes on the map.
The new teacher turned out to be somewhat stricter than the last.

short: by far the / such a / somewhat of a
notes: Card: peaks ' far' x7, ' such' x6, ' of' x6, ' called' x4; the pole's output promotes ' an', ' a', ' another'. Probes: 'by far the best' 0.77, 'somewhat of an' 0.71, 'such an envelope' 0.49, 'more of a' 0.32, 'called a' 0.26, 'quite a' 0.22; the same words without a following article: 'not far from' 0.01, 'As far as' 0.02, 'Such things' 0.15, 'somewhat tired' 0.08, 'Many of them' 0.01.
